proof: The delta document is versioned 5.0.0 and section 7 enumerates every superseded v1 to v4 claim, so a reader cannot treat two versions as concurrently true.
The companion checksum covers this manifest, so a silent second copy of the evidence fails verification.
The head binding is a content digest over the delta document and the validator pair, so a second copy of any bound artifact that differs by one byte is rejected by rule head_binding.
Fails closed on product-evidence schema validation or companion checksum mismatch.
Gaps whose target task has no PR record PR none rather than borrowing an unrelated PR number; unverified references are removed instead of being downgraded.

scripts/validate_twelve_loop_gap_evidence.py adds five fail-closed rejection rules. future_timestamp rejects any evidence_cut_at, validated_at, observed_at, record_log recorded_at, or required-check completed_at later than the check instant. head_binding rejects a bare 40-hex commit sha in validated_head_sha, a bound artifact whose sha256 has drifted, and a content digest that no longer matches the tree. record_log_ordering rejects non-increasing sequences and backwards timestamps. checks_bound_to_commits rejects a required check reported on a head that is not a recorded anchor commit. companion_checksum rejects a manifest whose bytes no longer match evidence.sha256.
Run against the rejected v4 manifest with --now 2026-07-26T21:49:00Z, the validator returns exactly the Human/Ops findings: two future_timestamp rejections and one head_binding rejection.

scripts/test_validate_twelve_loop_gap_evidence.py pins each rule with a mutation test and asserts the delivered manifest passes all five, so a future recut that reintroduces either defect fails in the repository test suite.
